notes: MCP TOOLS. Read rever-tools-api/src/tool.rs and utils.rs first: implement `Tool` for each tool (`def()` returns `ToolDef::new("<name>", "<description>", <schema>)` with the name as a string literal at that call, the description copied verbatim from the TypeScript because it is prompt text, and the schema being the zod schema converted to JSON Schema: same property names, types, enums, defaults, limits, descriptions and required list), and expose `pub fn register(registry: &mut ToolRegistry)` from lib.rs. Output text must equal the TypeScript's: same wording, same JSON shape and key order (serde_json's preserve_order feature is enabled in this crate, keep it). The CLI command spec (compile, describe, build request, extract, export) is already ported in rever-cli-spec, the macro guard and tool profiles in rever-tool-profile: use them as path dependencies. cli-exec.ts runs a saved command by sending its HTTP request through the repeater, which another agent is porting into a different crate right now: do not depend on it; define a small trait in this crate for sending one request (method, URL, headers, body in; status, headers, body out), looked up from `ctx.state::<T>()`, with a default implementation on reqwest with rustls-tls, so the real repeater can be plugged in later. Saved commands and macros persist under Electron's userData in the TypeScript: use `ctx.data_dir` with the same file names and JSON shapes. workflow-executor.ts runs macro and pipeline steps by calling other tools: run steps by looking tools up by name in a `ToolRegistry` handle kept in `ctx.state::<T>()` (the app fills it in after registering everything), applying the macro guard before each call exactly as the TypeScript does. Async: `call` returns a boxed future run on a tokio runtime; tests use #[tokio::test], a temporary data_dir, fake tools and a fake sender; no test may reach the internet. A tool file gets the `Port of` marker when all of its tools are registered.
